top_issues: Headline 'Total balance $222.99' sits above a 'Promised $122.99' line, so a first-time user can read the largest number as fully spendable when it is mostly a hub promise.
The 'Two colours, one rule' explainer card is prominent on first view but will be noise to a returning user and is not dismissible.
Bottom-left of the balances column has dead space under the rows, leaving the left column unbalanced.
fixes: Add a clear 'of which $182.99 is spendable now' caption directly under the headline balance.
Persist a dismissed state for the color explainer after first read.
Soften the split with a subheading and rebalance layout; add a compact risk line instead of a big card.

top_issues: Fee is shown as 'under 0.01 USDC', which is too vague to be a real decision input and differs from the precision used elsewhere.
'Up to 155.00 instantly' next to the amount field uses 'up to' wording that a cautious user may find ambiguous about the actual spendable cap.
The ROUTE pane and the 'YOUR ACCOUNT WITH H1' before/after pane are both on the right, causing some duplication of mental load.
fixes: Show an exact fee (e.g. '0.000025 USDC') with a one-line breakdown of base + bps.
Replace 'Up to 155.00' with 'Spendable now 155.00' to remove ambiguity.
Merge ROUTE into the account pane or push ROUTE below it so the before/after anchor is highest.

top_issues: Four export actions (Copy receipt, Download, Print/PDF) plus a primary 'Done' create choice overload on a confirmation that should be one tap.
The receipt modal covers the account changes it caused, so a user cannot verify the post-payment balance without closing it.
Proof hash is truncated (0x8c3213ba4...1399) with no copy affordance on the hash itself.
fixes: Make 'Done' the single prominent CTA and collapse Copy/Download/Print into one 'Export' menu.
Add a subtle 'view account' link inside the receipt that reveals the post-payment state.
Provide a copy-action on the truncated proof hash.

top_issues: 'Amount optional — 0.00' shows a zero amount, which can look like a bug or imply the receiver sets it, when actually the payer fills it in.
'45.50 capacity via H1' uses 'capacity', a technical term that civilians will not parse.
The note field placeholder 'What is this for?' adds an unused form field to a request flow.
fixes: Change 'Amount optional / 0.00' to 'The payer sets the amount' and drop the zero placeholder.
Add a plain-language tooltip for capacity ('how much can come in right now').
Hide the note field behind an 'add note' disclosure so the QR is the first thing seen.

top_issues: The swap screen stacks 'Prepare to receive', the collateral slider, and the credit-limit checkbox above the Swap button, which is three prerequisites before the single actionable action.
The price-ladder book dominates the right column and competes with the action column for attention.
The credit-limit request is pre-checked by default, so a user may extend credit without noticing.
The receive amount shows six decimals (0.039992) with no USD equivalent, making value hard to judge.
fixes: Reorder so the primary 'Swap' action is at top; collapse Prepare-to-receive into a confirmation step.
Make the book collapsible or secondary by default.
Make extending credit an explicit opt-in rather than pre-checked.
Show a USD value next to the receive amount.

top_issues: The receive amount 0.007998 WETH is shown with no USD value, so the user cannot judge it as a salary-sized transfer.
'LEGS' (1 Testnet, 2 Tron, 0 Clear) is novel jargon for a route; '0 Clear' is meaningless to a non-protocol person.
Decimal precision differs from the same-network swap (4 decimals here vs 6 there), an inconsistency.
A 'Prepare incoming capacity after confirmation' tooltip appears inline, introducing an extra prerequisite to a supposedly final action.
fixes: Show a USD equivalent next to the cross-network receive amount.
Rename 'LEGS' to 'Route steps' and title '0 Clear' as 'no refund risk'.
Use consistent decimal precision across swap screens.
Surface the incoming-capacity requirement as a clearly labeled pre-step, not a hover-only hint.

top_issues: The large '+130.00' is prominent but is 'they owe you', which a casual reader can mistake for spendable balance.
'They owe you uncovered $97.99 Cover it' uses 'uncovered' plus a 'Cover it' CTA that can alarm a user without context.
The two credit lines ('Their credit line to you 0.00' vs 'Your credit line to them 115.50') are accurate but the direction of exposure is not stated in plain language.
fixes: Label the big number 'they owe you (not spendable yet)'.
Explain 'uncovered' as 'what they promised but did not back with collateral'.
Add a plain-line phrase under the two credit lines: 'you let them owe you up to this much'.

top_issues: The dimmed overlay reduces legibility of the account panel while choosing dispute options, so the user cannot re-check claims mid-decision.
The dispute wording is a large block of prose ('2 sided... 1. You send... 2. They or you...') that is harder to scan than the account data itself.
Dispute options are not broken into short single-line actions.
fixes: Reduce overlay opacity so the account numbers stay readable during dispute.
Split the prose into short, bulleted single-line options.
Keep the disputed frame hash visible without scrolling.

top_issues: Status dots (settled/filled/open/created) are primarily color-only (green/orange/plain), risking inaccessible meaning for colorblind users.
The detail shows '-25.00 USDC' in a pink/red tint, which a nervous user may read as a loss rather than a direction.
'Export CSV' and the detail panel's 'Download proof' are two separate export affordances, splitting the audit mental model.
fixes: Add a text label next to every status dot and increase contrast between settled and filled.
Clarify the minus as 'sent' not 'lost' by adding a 'sent' glyph or label.
Unify export into one 'Export' action that includes both the statement and proof.

top_issues: This screen is functionally the same as 07-activity with a different selected row, so it does not add new information or a distinct detail view.
The status dot 'filled' vs 'settled' contrast is the same low-contrast issue as on the list view.
The frame number (#74) provides no ordering/sequence context for the user.
fixes: Add a per-frame drill-down (route steps, both signatures, pre/post balances) to make this a real detail view.
Strengthen the settled/filled differentiation.
Show a small sequence badge or relate the frame to the account timeline.

top_issues: 'Reveal recovery phrase', 'Lock' and 'Forget vault' sit side-by-side, so a misclick on 'Forget vault' could destroy the wallet with no confirm step.
The three vault actions are not visually distinguished by risk level.
The 'Design > Sample' preview restates a large balance that is unrelated to the user's real state, which can be momentarily confusing.
fixes: Add a confirmation dialog to 'Forget vault' and style it as a destructive (red) action separated from benign ones.
Order the vault actions by risk (reveal < lock < forget).
Label the design sample as 'preview' explicitly.

top_issues: The FROM and TO cards are identical (Wallet 0.00 / Reserve 40.00 / Account 130.00), so the direction of the move is visually ambiguous and both sides look the same.
'up to 40.00 USDC' refers to the selected From Reserve but is not attached to the card that explains the cap.
'Recipient entity: leave empty for yourself' requires understanding self-transfer semantics.
fixes: Differentiate source and destination cards (e.g. arrow direction, dimmed unavailable options).
Attach the cap directly under the selected From card.
Use a plain label like 'move to my own account' for the self-transfer option.

top_issues: The card grid (Sovereignty / Move / Assets / Lending / Ownership) has an empty slot after Lending, which looks like a broken layout.
'Where your money stands' repeats the Home breakdown without adding the at-risk nuance from Sovereignty.
The single H1 account card makes 'ACCOUNTS' look nearly empty on a multi-account runtime.
fixes: Fill the sixth slot (e.g. 'Disputes' or 'Evidence') or reflow the grid evenly.
Add a line that reconciles: '$197.99 total = $100.00 yours + $97.99 promised by H1'.
Hide the Accounts card entirely if only one account exists, or show it as a compact list.

top_issues: Two buttons look disabled simultaneously ('Extend credit limit' and 'Receive USDC from H1'), leaving no clear enabled next action.
'needs 54.500978 USDC more' is an over-precise number that is hard to read as an actionable balance.
'Depository may pull 0.00' is unexplained and reads as a risk with no context.
The Faucets section is dev-oriented (TRX/SUN/Token row) and noisy for an asset view.
fixes: Make the primary next action enabled and clearly labeled; explain the disabled reasons in one line.
Round 'needs X more' to two decimals with an exact toggle.
Replace 'May pull 0.00' with 'Depository can pull collateral from this wallet (currently $0) and explain what that means.
Move Faucets behind a 'testnet tools' disclosure.

top_issues: '100 basis points' is displayed as '= 100% per term', which is factually wrong (100 bps = 1.00%, not 100%) and is a serious data-legibility error.
The term selector is laid out across 1hour / 1day / 1month with the selected state, but no annualized rate is shown to compare terms.
'Interest you ask' labels the quotient, but the per-term vs annualized meaning is not distinguished.
fixes: Fix the conversion label: 100 bps = 1.00%, and put the exact percent on the button.
Show the effective annualized rate for each term.
Clarify 'per term' vs 'per year' with an explicit caption.

top_issues: The screen is sparse; the 'Take control of another entity' card is mostly empty dead space with 'Nothing to take over'.
The copy 'A lazy entity is identified by the hash of its board' is protocol jargon that does not help an owner.
Threshold 1 of 1 is shown without flagging the risk that a single key means no quorum.
fixes: Add a compact 'what this means' summary and a one-line risk note that 1-of-1 means one key controls the entity.
Fill the empty card with an explainer or a 'how to invite a co-signer' step.
Replate the lazy-entity copy with plain language.

top_issues: 'Enforceable right now $100.00' does not reconcile in one glance with Home's '$222.99' or Manage's '$197.99'; the user has to do mental arithmetic.
The Ledger panel shows a long runtime hash ('0x6c772...92ea') inline, which is technical noise.
'Can dispute without asking 1 of 1' is useful but is not given a definition of 'asking'.
fixes: Add a one-line reconciliation: 'of your $197.99 total, $100.00 is enforceable and $97.99 is promised by H1'.
Shorten the runtime hash in the Ledger with a copy affordance.
Add a tooltip for 'without asking' (no hub approval needed).

top_issues: The dense grid shows three headline cards ($197.99 / Yours on-chain $100.00 / At risk $97.99) plus '$157.99 | $48.30', giving multiple competing totals.
The single colored legend row (on-chain / reserve / secured / promised / you owe / credit room / in flight) spans the whole table and is hard to map to any one column.
The account-lane table has many columns (Account lane, Position, Secured, Promised, You owe, Send/Receive, Credit out) in a narrow space.
fixes: Group the three cards with a single 'reconciles to $197.99' caption.
Make the legend apply per column with a hover highlight.
Allow column hiding and horizontal scroll, and increase row height for legibility.

top_issues: Some palette descriptions are cryptic ('denie console' for Desk, 'keys, proofs, exposure' for Sovereignty), which undermines the discoverability the palette is meant to provide.
A blurred/dimmed desk behind the palette makes the backdrop noisy instead of calm.
The items mix product screens and concepts (Desk, Home) without a clear grouping.
fixes: Rewrite the cryptic descriptions into short plain phrases that mirror the screen titles.
Dim the backdrop more evenly (or blur stronger) so the palette reads as the foreground.
Group results into 'screens' and 'actions'.

overall.verdict: This is a genuinely protocol-honest, high-trust wallet: it shows enforceability vs promise, co-signed frames, credit lines, collateral and disputes with unusual precision, and the green/violet color rule is a rare example of a clean educational model. But it over-loads every non-trivial action (swap, cross-chain, dispute) with jargon and prerequisite steps, and there are a few correctness/show-stopping issues — a 100 basis-point rate rendered as '100%' and competing headline totals — that would confuse even a careful user.
priority_fixes: Fix the Lending bps label (100 bps = 1.00%, not 100%) and show the annualized rate.
Make the headline balance honest: on Home add 'of which $182.99 is spendable now', and on Account label the big number 'they owe you (not spendable yet)'.
Cut swap/decision load: put the primary action at the top, collapse Prepare-to-receive and the book by default, and show a USD value next to every receive and cross-chain amount.
Add guardrails and accessibility: a confirm step plus destructive styling on 'Forget vault', and text labels next to every status dot so meaning is never color-only.
Reconcile the multiple totals (Home / Manage / Sovereignty / Desk) into one plain-language line so 'yours vs enforceable vs promised' is a single mental model.

Recent-list status dots rely partly on color
The fee on Pay is vague ('under 0.01 USDC') and several label rows are small

personas.name: Jamal

personas.name: Priya

Settled/open rely on small colored dots
Closing-time reconcile needs a group-by-settled view for the list
